mock.subject: maths
mock.title: Chain rule
mock.ai1: I know a bit of differentiation. But where does the name “chain rule” come from? What's the chain?
mock.me1: Think of nested functions: f(g(x)). You take the derivative of the outer one and multiply by the derivative of the inner. Like links in a chain.
mock.ai2: Okay, links make sense. But why do we multiply instead of add? Can you show me with an example?
mock.gap: gap: why we multiply isn't explained
mock.note: Your student keeps getting stuck on “why”. Try explaining with cause and effect.

ters.title: Every learning app teaches you. Tutorla wants to learn.
ters.quote: Students assume they understood. Real understanding only shows up when you try to explain it to someone — that's when you find out which step you memorised.
ters.gapNote: Practice tests catch the gap but never show you why.

nasil.title: A session in four steps
nasil.s1d: Exam mode, subject, topic. YKS → maths → derivatives → chain rule.
nasil.s2d: Curious, sceptical or impatient. Each one pushes you from a different side.
nasil.s3d: Type, talk, draw on the board or upload a photo of your notebook. Your student listens and asks.
nasil.s4d: The understanding map marks every concept. The session note tells you how you explained.

neden.title: We learn by teaching.
neden.c1d: If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it yet. Tutorla tests exactly that, every session.
neden.c2d: Students who prepare to teach learn more deeply than students who prepare for a test. The research keeps showing it.
neden.c3d: Seneca, two thousand years ago: by teaching, we learn. That line is where the brand starts.
neden.examsText: There is no other app that speaks Turkish, knows the YKS curriculum, and wants to learn from you instead of teaching you. That intersection is empty — Tutorla is being built there.

guide.title: How to use Tutorla
guide.intro: Every part of the product, explained in order: how a session works, what the marks on your understanding map mean, and everything else. In a hurry? Start the tour and let it point at the real interface.

ters.p1: Thinking you know a topic and being able to explain it are not the same thing. Reading feels smooth; explaining stops you mid-sentence. That stop is exactly where the gap is.
ters.p2: Tutorla exists to make that visible. The AI here isn't a teacher, it's a curious student: it asks, it says what it didn't follow, it pushes you to explain. It never hands you the answer — handing you the answer would close the very place where learning happens.
ters.p3: Education research calls this the protégé effect: students who prepare to teach learn more deeply than students who prepare for a test.

seans.p1: My lessons → exam → subject → topic. The moment you open a topic a session starts and your student asks its first question. Here's a shortened real session:
seans.d1: Could you explain the "implicit function" part? I didn't follow it at all.
seans.d2: In implicit differentiation we differentiate both sides with respect to x. Since y depends on x, differentiating y brings in a dy/dx factor.
seans.dm: Causality — you linked it with “because”, it didn't sound memorised.
seans.d3: But why isn't the derivative of y just 1? What happened there?
seans.dg: gap: why the chain rule applies to y wasn't explained
seans.p2: Notice the student doesn't answer; it points at what's missing. Explain that gap and the concept is marked as settled, lifting the percentage on your map.
seans.p3: When you finish, a short note is written underneath: what you explained and how. You can return to an unfinished session from History, and your draft survives a closed tab.

harita.p1: The right-hand panel lists the topic's concepts. Each is in one of three states:
harita.l2: gap — you explained it but something was missing
harita.l3: settled — you explained enough to close the student's question
harita.p2: The percentage isn't stored; it's derived every time as settled ÷ total. No counter drift: what you see is the real state.
harita.p3: On phones the map lives in a collapsible strip under the title rather than a side panel — it's the core feedback, so it stays within reach.

kanit.p1: Learning evidence — what you learned. If a concept was a gap first and settled later, it's marked “closed by teaching”. That count is the measurable trace of the protégé effect.
kanit.p2: Behaviour evidence — how you taught. Five things get recorded as you explain: persistence, causality, concreteness, simplification, curiosity. Not a grade — a concrete record that replaces the vague feeling of “I studied well today”.
kanit.p3: Neither replaces the other: one shows what you learned, the other how.

sokratik.p1: The opposite of the main mode: it asks, you think. It won't give you the answer, it narrows in with questions. Warming up in Socratic mode before teaching a shaky topic is a good order.

mufredat.p1: Preparing for an exam that isn't listed? My lessons → “Add exam”. Then write your own subjects, topics and concepts — your understanding map is built from those concepts. You can upload curriculum documents (PDF, text, images) too.
mufredat.p2: The official curriculum (YKS) can't be edited; only exams you added yourself.

akis.p1: Share where you got stuck, read how others explained it. Posts with photos, GIFs and emoji; comments and replies; reactions and bookmarks. Bookmarks collect in their own tab.
akis.p2: If a post or a person bothers you there's reporting and blocking: a blocked person's content disappears from your feed entirely.

mesaj.p1: One-to-one chat to work through a topic together. Open someone's profile, hit “Send a message”. Messages arrive instantly, no refresh needed, and unread counts show on the navbar badge.

arama.p1: The magnifier or ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows). Topics, concepts, people, posts and exams in one box. Hit a topic and you continue an open session or start a new one.
arama.k5: In a session ⏎ — send, ⇧⏎ — new line

profil.p1: The better your student knows you, the sharper its questions: your year, track, target department, strong and weak subjects. Most fields suggest options without locking you into them — you can always type your own.
profil.p2: Upload and crop a profile photo, rotate it, or take one with your camera. If you'd rather stay private, the privacy switch is at the bottom.

ai.t: 11. An honest note: the AI isn't connected yet
ai.p1: Right now your student's questions come from hand-written rules and are marked in the interface with a “scripted student” badge. Once Claude is connected the questions will be generated from what you actually wrote; the flow stays the same.
ai.p2: Likewise, curriculum documents you upload are stored but not processed yet.

tips.t: Three tips to get more out of it
tips.a: Explain with cause and effect, not short statements. Sentences with “because” surface gaps faster.
tips.b: When the student says it didn't follow, don't repeat the sentence — give an example. Concrete examples beat repeating a definition.
tips.c: See a session through to the end. The session note is only written when you finish, and it's usually the most useful feedback.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: You pick a topic and explain it to the AI. It acts like a curious student — asking questions and marking the gaps in your explanation. It never hands you the answer; it makes what's missing visible.
faq.a2: No — the opposite. Tutorla won't answer for you; it asks you to explain. The point isn't finishing the task, it's seeing whether you actually understood.
faq.a3: The YKS curriculum is loaded: maths, physics, chemistry, biology, Turkish, literature, history, geography, philosophy, religious studies and English. LGS, KPSS, DGS, ALES, SAT and TÜBİTAK are next. You can also add your own exam and curriculum.
faq.a4: We're in closed testing and it's free. Pricing isn't decided yet; when it is, the early-access list hears first.
faq.a5: Your sessions and progress are visible only to you — locked down at the database level. You can make your profile fully private. Servers are in Frankfurt.
faq.a6: Not yet. The student currently runs on hand-written rules and is labelled “scripted student” in the interface. We're working on the persona; it'll take over when it's ready.

pricing.title: Free for now
pricing.body: We're in closed testing. Everything is free and unlimited during this period. When we settle on pricing, the early-access list hears first — and gets its own terms.
